ideas.hypothesis: Stocks trading at their recent high after a strong run keep drifting up because investors anchor on the high and under-react to the good news behind the run.
ideas.rule: Entry: below_3m_high >= -1.0% AND d20 >= +10% AND entry cost <= 1.5%. If more than 2 names qualify on a day, buy only the 2 with the largest d20. Size: max whole shares under the 25% cap. Horizon 20 trading days; exit at horizon or the -8% stop. No re-entry in a name already held.
ideas.source: George & Hwang (2004), The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing, Journal of Finance; adapted to the 3-month high available in the features
ideas.note: New. First signal day: AZN, BAYN, GSK, NOVN, SAN.PA all qualify on price; AZN fails the cost filter (2.26%); BAYN and SAN.PA have the largest d20. All signals are pharma, so the results are exposed to one sector.

ideas.hypothesis: After a company raises its forecast or reports results above expectations, the price keeps drifting in the direction of the news for days because investors under-react to earnings information.
ideas.rule: Entry: a headline on the decision day that names the company and says it raised its forecast/guidance/outlook or beat results expectations, AND d1 >= +2% (the market confirms the news as positive), AND entry cost <= 1.5%. Horizon 10 trading days; exit at horizon or the -8% stop. Analyst rating/target changes and regulatory approvals do not count.
ideas.source: Bernard & Thomas (1989), Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift; Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok (1996), Momentum Strategies
ideas.note: New. First signal: IFX.DE raised its data-centre revenue forecast to nearly 4 bn EUR, d1 +2.59%.

ideas.hypothesis: A large one-day drop without company-specific news is often liquidity or flow driven and partly reverses within days, while drops with news do not.
ideas.rule: Entry: d1 <= -3.0% AND no headline on the decision day naming the company (theme-wide commodity headlines are allowed) AND the stock's main driver (oil for oil_gas, gold for gold_miners, copper for copper_uranium, ^STOXX50E otherwise) moved less than half as much as the stock, AND entry cost <= 1.5%. Horizon 3 trading days; exit at horizon or the -8% stop.
ideas.source: Jegadeesh (1990), Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns; Lehmann (1990); Chan (2003), Stock price reaction to news and no-news
